title: One God, three persons
hookLine: Father, Son and Holy Spirit: one God in a communion of love

cards: In a Russian monastery, around six hundred years ago, a monk named Andrei Rublev painted an icon of God as Trinity. Three angels sit around a table, under a tree.
It's the Genesis story of three visitors at Abraham's tent. They look almost identical, long-winged and gentle-faced, each head tilting toward the others. Nobody sits at the head of the table.
Their hands and eyes make a circle. And at the front, facing you, there's an open place, as if someone has been invited in. Christians have looked at it for centuries to glimpse today's word.

teach.b: Trinity comes from the Latin trinitas, a three-in-oneness. A North African writer named Tertullian used it around the year 200. Surprise: the word isn't in the Bible.
The three names are, again and again. At Jesus's baptism: the Son in the water, the Spirit like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven.
At the end of Matthew, Jesus sends his friends out, "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." Name, singular. Three, and one.
Paul ends a letter with a blessing still said in churches: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all."
Christians say the Trinity is one God in three persons: not three gods, and not one God wearing three masks.
The councils spent decades finding words for it, and Christians are the first to call it a mystery.

People try pictures, water as ice, liquid and steam, or a three-leaf shamrock, but theologians usually say every picture goes wrong somewhere. So why hold it at all? One answer starts from First John: God is love.

teach.h: GOD IS LOVE, SO GOD IS COMMUNION.
teach.b: Love needs someone to love, the reasoning goes.

teach.h: THE COMMUNION OF THE HOLY GHOST.
teach.b: If God is Trinity, then before anything was made, God was already a communion: giving, receiving, sharing, forever. That's what Rublev painted: a circle of love, with a place left open.

Some Christians, such as Unitarians, Jehovah's Witnesses and Latter-day Saints, understand God differently. For the Catholic, Orthodox and historic Protestant churches, the Trinity is at the center of the faith.

how: Many Christians make the sign of the cross "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit," and many churches celebrate Trinity Sunday, the Sunday after Pentecost.

games.q: you're a monk in Russia, around 1420, asked to paint God as Trinity. what do you paint?
o: an old man, a young man and a dove.
three angels at Abraham's table, with an open place.
a triangle with an eye in it.
games.why: Rublev painted the three visitors from Genesis 18 at one table, their gazes making a circle, and a place left open facing you.

practice: Think of three people who love each other, maybe you and two friends, a parent and two children, and picture them at one table. Notice how the love doesn't split into pieces; it goes round, and gets bigger with each person.
If you pray, use Paul's blessing: the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost. If you don't, rest in the picture of that table.
